candidates.subject: test: reproduce a stale worker resolving a re-picked job (#957)
candidates.read: commit message, `git show --stat`, the diff of pgqueuer/ and RELEASE.md/docs hunks, docs/guides/reliability.md hunk, test/test_stale_worker_fencing.py (whole file)
candidates.note: Database-mediated and public (a stale worker resolving a job another worker re-picked after the heartbeat timeout). E3: the precondition is a worker that stays alive but sends no heartbeat for heartbeat_timeout of wall-clock time (the maintainers' test backdates the heartbeat with direct SQL). Under the lockstep coordinator a handler that blocks its event loop blocks every actor (no grants while any actor computes), so the takeover is reachable only by a gate that holds every statement of one worker until another claims; that is a forced schedule, not the stepping seam's exploration, and was not built in this sprint. Recorded as failing E3 (a contestable judgement: a holding gate might make it buildable as a forced-schedule case) rather than claimed.

candidates.subject: fix(qm): release a retried job's context before re-queueing it (#913)
candidates.read: commit message, `git show --stat`, the diff of pgqueuer/ and RELEASE.md/docs hunks, test/test_retry_requeue.py hunk
candidates.note: A retried job (RetryRequested, delay 0) re-picked by its own worker before the first dispatch task's done callback dropped its context, then skipped. The window is between a task's done-callback and the same worker's next dequeue result: an event-loop interleaving inside one process, which the seam doesn't control (CAPABILITY_MATRIX: grants are controlled, in-process task timing is not). It is also a liveness delay that stale recovery eventually ends.
